A_target.statement:
Let $T: V \to W$ be a [[Definition:Linear Transformation|linear transformation]] with $V$ [[Definition:Dimension of Vector Space|finite-dimensional]].
Then:
:$\dim V = \map \dim {\map \ker T} + \map \rank T$

B_source.statement:
Let $T: V \to W$ be a [[Definition:Linear Transformation|linear transformation]].
Then:
:$V / \map \ker T \cong \Img T$

validity_conditions: V finite-dimensional, so all dimensions are finite and dim(V/U) = dim V - dim U holds for a subspace U.
Isomorphic finite-dimensional spaces have equal dimension, so dim(V/ker T) = dim(im T).
Substituting dim(V/ker T) = dim V - dim(ker T) yields rank-nullity - a dimension count of the iso theorem.
proof_plan:
By the [[First Isomorphism Theorem for Vector Spaces]]:
:$V / \map \ker T \cong \Img T$

Isomorphic spaces have equal dimension:
:$\map \dim {V / \map \ker T} = \map \dim {\Img T} = \map \rank T$

By [[Dimension of Quotient Space]]:
:$\map \dim {V / \map \ker T} = \dim V - \map \dim {\map \ker T}$

Rearranging:
:$\dim V = \map \dim {\map \ker T} + \map \rank T$
which is the [[Rank-Nullity Theorem]].
{{qed}}
